business_scope.primary_industry_name: Offshore Building Information Modeling (BIM) and Structural Drafting

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: South Africa (unitary national registry; no separate sub-state business registry)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid — Roman-Dutch civilist foundations overlaid with English Common Law; constitutional supremacy under the Constitution, 1996; corporate law governed nationally by the Companies Act 71 of 2008 and Companies Regulations, 2011
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: South Africa–United States Convention for the Avoidance of Double Taxation (2001)
South Africa–United Kingdom Double Taxation Agreement (as amended 2022)
SADC Protocol on Finance and Investment (Annex 1 on Investment Promotion)
African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) Agreement — services and engineering professional mobility

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Companies Act 71 of 2008 as amended by the General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Terrorism Financing) Amendment Act 22 of 2022 and the Companies Amendment Act 16 of 2024 (beneficial ownership regime in ss 56A–56D); Companies Regulations 2011 (Reg 32–33, Forms CoR 9.3 and CoR 15.1E); Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001 (FICA) as amended by the FIC Amendment Act 1 of 2017 (s 21B, s 22A, Schedule 1); Protection of Constitutional Democracy against Terrorism and Related Activities Act 33 of 2004 (POCDATARA) targeted financial sanctions; CIPC Beneficial Ownership Register Directive (2023). South African statutory UBO disclosure threshold for the company register is 5% of issued securities or voting rights (Companies Act s 1 definition of 'beneficial owner'), whereas FICA CDD/EDD triggers apply at the 25% level for accountable institutions.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access — the CIPC Beneficial Ownership Register is filed with CIPC at incorporation and on any change and is accessible to FIC, SARS, SAPS, the Special Investigating Unit (SIU), the NPA and other authorised authorities; it is not publicly searchable and nominee arrangements remain legally permissible only where the underlying natural-person beneficial owner is disclosed to CIPC.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Full-color certified copy of passport of each founding director and shareholder (natural persons)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport-issuing authority in the director's/shareholder's country of nationality or residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (if country of issue is an apostille signatory) OR Consular Legalization at the South African mission (non-signatory jurisdictions)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Police clearance / certificate of good conduct for each director and beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National police or criminal records authority of the country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential or business address (utility bill or regulated bank statement, dated within 3 months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or regulated bank in the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy by local notary + Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency / Good Standing of any corporate shareholder (juristic beneficial-owner chain evidence)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry or registered agent of the shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization; certified English translation where the original is in a non-English script

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming source of funds and standing of the founding shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Originating regulated bank of the founding shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy + Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all directors, shareholders and indirect beneficial owners against OFAC SDN, UN Security Council consolidated lists, EU/UK consolidated sanctions, and South African targeted financial sanctions administered by FIC under POCDATARA; FICA risk-based CDD requires identification and verification of beneficial owners, with enhanced due diligence where a PEP (domestic or foreign), a family member or a close associate of a PEP holds 5% or more; for this Low_Risk_Standard engineering CAD/BIM outsourcing profile, standard CDD applies, but CIPC requires the beneficial ownership declaration (Form CoR 15.1E) to be lodged within 10 business days of incorporation and updated within 10 business days of any change.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.registered_office_and_commercial_substan: Section 23(3) of the Companies Act mandates that a company continuously maintain a registered office with a physical street address in South Africa at which legal process may be served during ordinary business hours; a serviced/virtual-office physical address is permissible for a CAD/BIM exporter provided the provider accepts statutory process and is not a mere post-office box; the likely physical-inspection risk within the first 36 months is assessed at 15–25% given the Low_Risk_Standard AML profile, though the presence of a co-working address and absence of a resident natural-person director may raise SARS/FIC verification flags.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: CIPC BizPortal (Companies and Intellectual Property Commission e-services — https://eservices.cipc.co.za); Form CoR 9.1 (Reservation of Name) filed electronically; supplementary name-reconsideration matters handled via the CIPC Customer Contact Centre and Companies Tribunal e-filing
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The reserved company name must be expressed in Latin script; African-language and foreign-language components are accepted only in romanised transliteration; CIPC will not register names containing non-Latin characters (e.g. Chinese characters) — a certified transliteration and, where relevant, a sworn translation of the proposed name and its business meaning must accompany the CoR 9.1 filing; the name must not be offensive, contrary to public policy, or confusingly similar to an existing registered name or trademark under s 11(2) of the Companies Act.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank / Building Society / Finance / Financial Services (FSCA licensing condition)
Trust / Trustee / Retirement Fund (financial-sector regulatory approval)
University / College / School (Department of Higher Education approval)
Municipal / Government / Republic / National / Ministerial (state-authority consent)
Council / Board / Chamber of Mines / Association / Institute (member-body or ministerial approval)

Professional Engineer / Consulting Engineer / Civil Engineer (ECSA registration required under the Engineering Profession Act 46 of 2000; CIPC will require an ECSA letter where the token implies the regulated practice of professional engineering)
Attorney / Legal / Notary / Advocate (Legal Practice Act 28 of 2014 permission)
Incorporated / Limited / Co-operative / Close Corporation (restricted designations for other statutory legal forms)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Under Regulation 13 of the Companies Regulations 2011, CIPC reserves a name for six months; there is no statutory extension, and upon expiry a fresh CoR 9.1 may be filed with the same name if still available. On rejection, CIPC issues a Notice of Refusal stating the s 11 grounds; the applicant may within 10 business days lodge a written reconsideration request with CIPC, attaching a revised name or a legal motivation; if CIPC maintains the refusal, the applicant may apply to the Companies Tribunal under s 160 of the Companies Act (Form CTR 142) within 20 business days of the refusal decision, or file an alternative name from the CoR 9.1 priority list; judicial review under s 161 of the Companies Act remains the final administrative-law avenue.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens_note: For an engineering-outsourcing entity, the words 'Engineering' or 'Structural' without the preceding 'Professional' or 'Consulting' marker generally avoid the ECSA pre-clearance triggers; nonetheless, prudent due diligence requires an ECSA letter of non-objection where the name contains 'Engineer' or 'Engineering'.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted with a material caveat: the registered office must be a genuine physical street address in South Africa where legal documents and statutory process can be served during ordinary business hours; a serviced or virtual office is commercially acceptable for this remote CAD/BIM business model, but the service provider must formally accept service of process, maintain business-hours reception, and provide practical access by SARS/CIPC inspectors; a P.O. Box is statutorily insufficient. The company must also appoint a natural-person public officer resident in South Africa for SARS purposes within the incorporation timeline.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: LOW_MODERATE — quantified at 15–25% probability of an unannounced physical inspection within the first 36 months; the stated Low_Risk_Standard AML tier reduces priority, yet CIPC annual-return verification, SARS VAT/PIT registration reviews, and FIC compliance audits may impose a desktop verification first and a physical visit where the registered address is a co-working/virtual office or where the public officer is not physically present at the registered office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.key_substance_evidence: Retained records should evidence the active operational substance of the CAD/BIM practice: international client contracts, software licences (Autodesk/Bentley suites), invoicing and payment rails (wire transfer, Wise), director decision logs, and the South African bank account linked to the registered office; absence of such substance data at the pre-incorporation stage elevates inspection risk and may delay bank account activation.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff — CIPC 2024/25 fee schedule: ZAR 50 online; market agent-handling rate ZAR 250–750

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: CIPC incorporation registration fee — private company (Pty) Ltd with standard MOI (CoR 14.1 / CoR 15.1A)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff — CIPC 2024/25 online e-services fee: ZAR 175; expedited/same-day processing: ZAR 350

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Beneficial ownership register (BOR) filing with CIPC at incorporation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff — ZAR 50 per online filing under Regulation 32, Companies Regulations 2011

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Customised Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI) drafting — risk-limitation provisions, shareholder class rights, director authority thresholds
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for SME incorporation: ZAR 3,500–7,500 plus VAT; standard CIPC banking-model MOI included in incorporation fee, custom drafting billed separately

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation UBO piercing, PEP/OFAC/UN sanctions screening, and FICA-aligned CDD file compilation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark: ZAR 8,000–15,000 for multi-jurisdictional desktop screening (World-Check, LexisNexis or equivalent datasets) and source-of-funds verification

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and Hague Apostille / consular legalization bundle — passports, police clearances, address proof, incumbency, and bank reference (estimated 4–6 foreign-origin documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public and apostille/consular authority in the shareholders'/directors' countries of origin
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing notarial and apostille tariffs: US$35–120 per document per jurisdiction; South African mission consular legalization fees where the Hague Convention does not apply

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translation and Latin-script transliteration of non-English founding documents (if applicable)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Sworn translator in country of origin or South Africa
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market rate ZAR 600–1,800 per notarised translation unit

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office — 12-month serviced physical street address subscription with statutory-process acceptance
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Serviced office provider in the target South African business district
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark ZAR 150–350 per month depending on city and service tier; excludes co-working desk rental

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: SARS and regulatory tax registration — income tax, VAT (voluntary), PAYE placeholder, and public-officer appointment
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark ZAR 1,500–2,500 for a complete tax registration engagement excluding VAT

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing courier tariff per dossier bundle, service class and origin region

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008, as amended (including the Companies Amendment Acts 16 and 17 of 2024 when in force); key provisions: s 13(1) (incorporation), s 14 (registration procedure), s 15 (Memorandum of Incorporation), s 19(1)(b) (separate legal personality), s 66 (board of directors), s 70 (first directors), and s 84 (financial oversight).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), an agency of the Department of Trade, Industry and Competition (the dtic); dtic Campus, 77 Meintjies Street, Sunnyside, Pretoria; filings made through the CIPC e-Services portal at www.cipc.co.za.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1) together with the Memorandum of Incorporation (standard Form CoR 15.1 or bespoke MOI) and written consents of the first directors, lodged electronically via CIPC e-Services.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up or authorised capital: the Companies Act 71 of 2008 abolished par value and minimum capital requirements. The incorporators may allot 100 no-par-value ordinary shares at R1.00 each (total R100.00); no escrow account or capital verification is required by CIPC.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME] (PTY) LTD. RESOLVED, as an ordinary resolution of the first board of directors, that: 1. The subscription of 100 ordinary shares at R1.00 each is accepted, allotted and issued fully paid; 2. The Memorandum of Incorporation is confirmed and adopted; 3. The registered office is fixed at 2nd Floor, The Firs, 8 Cradock Avenue, Rosebank, Johannesburg, 2196; 4. [Director Name] is appointed sole director and [Secretary Name] is appointed company secretary, each empowered to open banking accounts, execute contracts and instruct professional advisers; and 5. Directors endorse the CIPC incorporation filing and payment of prescribed fees. Passed unanimously.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log on to CIPC e-Services, select 'Name Clearance', submit Form CoR 9.1 with up to three proposed names in priority order and a brief statement of the main business, pay the prescribed fee electronically, and download the printed Name Clearance Certificate. The name is reserved for six months from the date of clearance.
required_dossiers: Form CoR 9.1 (application for reservation of name)
Certified copy of applicant identity document or passport
Proof of payment of name reservation fee
List of three proposed company names in priority order
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused under s 11 read with s 14(2) of the Companies Act, the applicant may file a formal objection with CIPC under Regulation 13, submit additional alternative names, or proceed with incorporation using a shortened variation of the proposed name and later effect a name change.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare the Notice of Incorporation and Memorandum of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC online filing system or a licensed company registration practitioner/attorney acting as agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form CoR 14.1 (Notice of Incorporation) stating the company name, principal business (ISIC 7110 engineering design and BIM services), registered office address, number of directors, and financial year-end. Attach the standard Memorandum of Incorporation (CoR 15.1) or a bespoke MOI signed by every incorporator, and obtain signed written consents from each of the first directors in accordance with s 66(4).
required_dossiers: Form CoR 14.1 (Notice of Incorporation)
Form CoR 15.1 or bespoke Memorandum of Incorporation
Written consent of each first director (Form CoR 14.2 / signed consent)
Certified copies of identity documents of incorporators and directors
Registered office consent letter signed by the property owner or managing agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: CIPC will issue a query notice listing defects in the forms or consents. The applicant must respond via e-Services within the stated period with corrected documents; if the MOI contains clauses not compliant with the Companies Act, redraft and refile, or apply to the Companies Tribunal for relief.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit incorporation application to CIPC and pay prescribed fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC e-Services 'Register a Company' module; physical lodgement: CIPC, dtic Campus, 77 Meintjies Street, Sunnyside, Pretoria
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the completed CoR 14.1 and MOI into the electronic registration workflow, pay the registration fee by debit/card or eFiling, and submit. CIPC will verify the name, check the MOI, register the company under s 14, allocate the company registration number (YYYY/XXXXXX/07), and issue the Certificate of Incorporation.
required_dossiers: Form CoR 14.1 (Notice of Incorporation)
Memorandum of Incorporation (CoR 15.1)
Proof of payment of incorporation fee
Name Clearance Certificate (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected or queried, respond to the CIPC query within the stipulated period with corrected information; if rejection persists, apply to the Companies Tribunal for review under s 14(16) or restart the process with a corrected MOI and new fee payment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Hold first board meeting, allot shares, adopt registered office, appoint officers and file beneficial ownership records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of directors; CIPC beneficial ownership registry within e-Services
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting and pass the written First Board Resolution adopting the MOI, fixing the registered office, accepting the share subscription, allotting 100 ordinary shares, and appointing officers. Maintain the register of members (s 50), register of directors (s 52), and the beneficial ownership register under s 56B of the Companies Act, and file the mandatory beneficial ownership declaration with CIPC.
required_dossiers: First Board Resolution (share allotment and registered office)
Share certificates for each subscriber
Register of members and register of directors
Beneficial ownership register and CIPC beneficial ownership filing
Notice of registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC issues a query on the beneficial ownership filing, correct the data and refile immediately, as failure to file is an offence. Any defect in the share allotment can be cured by a subsequent directors' resolution; late filings may be rectified by paying the applicable administrative fee to CIPC.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for tax and employment levies with SARS and the Department of Employment and Labour
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS eFiling: www.sarsefiling.co.za); Compensation Fund at the Department of Employment and Labour
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: SARS automatically links income tax registration to the CIPC incorporation and issues a tax reference number. Register for VAT on SARS eFiling if taxable supplies exceed or are expected to exceed R1 million per annum. Upon hiring employees, register as an employer for PAYE, UIF and SDL, and register with the Compensation Fund for COIDA coverage. File provisional tax returns and maintain required accounting records.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation (CoR 14.3)
Memorandum of Incorporation
Directors' certified identity documents
Bank account details (once opened)
Projected revenue statement for VAT threshold assessment
SARS VAT101 and EMP101 registration forms (as applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SARS fails to issue a tax reference number or queries the registration, submit a statement of account and incorporation certificate via eFiling or the SARS branch, and escalate to the SARS contact centre. Late registration attracts penalties under the Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011; file a voluntary disclosure or condonation application as appropriate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open a corporate bank account and complete AML/KYC verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed South African bank under the Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001 (e.g., Standard Bank, ABSA, FNB, Nedbank)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the Certificate of Incorporation, MOI, First Board Resolution appointing signatories, beneficial ownership schedule, and certified identification documents. The bank conducts Customer Due Diligence, FATCA/CRS classification, and source-of-funds verification, and opens a corporate account supporting wire transfers and Wise payment rails for the offshore BIM/CAD engineering client base.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation (CoR 14.3)
Memorandum of Incorporation
First Board Resolution (account opening and signatories)
Certified identity documents and residential addresses of directors and beneficial owners
Beneficial ownership register
SARS income tax reference number
Short business profile and anticipated transaction flows
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank raises an enhanced due diligence query, provide a sworn source-of-wealth statement, underlying client contracts, and projected cash flows. If the bank declines without statutory justification, escalate to the Financial Intelligence Centre Complaints mechanism or approach an alternative licenced bank; ensure RICA documentation is completed for account facilities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain premises-related municipal, fire and occupational health and safety clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local municipality (e.g., City of Johannesburg Fire Services and Planning Department); Department of Employment and Labour
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For the leased office premises, confirm that no municipal trading licence is required for an office-based engineering CAD and BIM consultancy. Obtain a fire certificate of compliance from the municipal fire protection services and the landlord's certificate of occupancy; conduct a baseline occupational health and safety risk assessment under the Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993 and register the workplace with the Department of Employment and Labour if required.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement for the registered office
Certificate of occupancy issued by the landlord
Fire compliance certificate from municipal fire services
Baseline OHS risk assessment
Electrical and structural compliance certificates (as applicable)
Department of Employment and Labour workplace registration (if required)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality issues a notice of unlicensed or non-compliant activity, apply for the relevant temporary or full municipal business licence or submit a formal exemption demonstrating that CAD drafting is not a listed licensed activity. For OHS non-compliance, remedy the identified hazards and submit an abatement plan to the Department of Employment and Labour.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — no industrial or manufacturing licence is required for an office-based engineering CAD and BIM consultancy. Professional registration with the Engineering Council of South Africa (ECSA) under the Engineering Profession Act 46 of 2000 may apply only to reserved engineering work performed by registered natural persons, not to the corporate entity itself.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable. The activity (ISIC 7110 offshore structural drafting and BIM services) is not a listed licensed activity under the National Business Licensing framework; any city-specific trading licence by-law (e.g., City of Johannesburg Business Licensing By-law) applies only to enumerated activities such as food handling, accommodation or special risk trades.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE), with provincial environmental authorities for any future listed activity
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no environmental authorisation is required for an administrative office tenancy; the activity does not appear in Listing Notices 1, 2 or 3 of the Environmental Impact Assessment Regulations, 2014, under the National Environmental Management Act 107 of 1998
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable for pure office operations. If the company later installs diesel backup generators or evaporative cooling equipment, compliance with the National Environmental Management: Air Quality Act 39 of 2004 (appointment lists and emission limits for VOCs, NOx and particulates) and municipal wastewater bylaws (pH 5.5–9.5, COD under 250 mg/L, suspended solids under 25 mg/L) would become mandatory.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate and certificate of compliance issued by municipal fire protection services under the National Building Regulations (Building Standards Act 103 of 1977); certificate of occupancy and structural load certification from the landlord for the leased office; occupational health and safety clearance under the Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993, including a baseline risk assessment, emergency evacuation plan, and notification of the Department of Employment and Labour for any workplace with employees.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS); statutory self-service portal is SARS eFiling (https://www.sarsefiling.co.za)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign and domestic entities must first complete incorporation or branch registration with the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC); thereafter obtain an Income Tax reference number via SARS eFiling or a SARS branch using the IT150/IT144 registration forms and appointing a Public Officer who must be resident in South Africa; a separate VAT101 application and turnover-declaration evidence are required for VAT registration; the same reference number governs PAYE, VAT, customs, and income tax account codes upon activation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box regime exists in South Africa. Relevant statutory elections include: (i) Small Business Corporation status under section 12E of the Income Tax Act for qualifying companies with gross income below ZAR 20 million; (ii) Hybrid debt/equity classification elections under sections 8F/8FA; (iii) Dividend access/declaration elections; (iv) Election to compute capital gains under IFRS versus tax-basis recognition; (v) Section 11D Research and Development intensive-filings; and (vi) Binding General Rulings or Advance Tax Rulings can be applied-for to fix tax characterisation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991, administered by SARS
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Compulsory registration when taxable supplies exceed or are reasonably expected to exceed ZAR 1,000,000 in a rolling 12-month period; voluntary registration permitted from ZAR 50,000 for qualifying suppliers; foreign suppliers of prescribed electronic services registered separately under special rules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: South Africa does not currently enforce real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or mandatory API clearance. VAT invoices must however satisfy section 20 of the VAT Act inclusive of supplier name, VAT number, invoice number, date, full description, consideration, and tax fraction. SARS eFiling supports electronic submissions, and a voluntary Peppol-based e-invoicing framework is being introduced; no immediate fiscal-stamping API is mandatory.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is claimable for exported goods under section 11(1)(a) of the VAT Act and for exported services under section 11(2)(l) where services are physically rendered outside South Africa, or under section 11(2)(m) where services are supplied to a non-resident who is not in South Africa at the time of supply, the services are not directly connected to land or movable property inside South Africa, and the services are not consumed or used in South Africa. Cross-border BIM/CAD engineering services supplied by a South African Pty Ltd to non-resident clients with offshore deliverables and no local nexus qualify, subject to retention of contract, non-residency proof, detailed scope of work, and evidence that intellectual effort and final use occur outside South Africa.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD500) and SARS customs clearance approval for physical goods movement
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing physical dispatch from South Africa when goods accompany the services
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) issued by an Authorised Dealer / bank SWIFT MT103 or equivalent telex transfer evidence proving repatriation of export proceeds to South Africa
Signed service agreement stating the non-resident recipient, overseas place of supply, and absence of South African supply nexus
Detailed invoice with the zero-rated VAT code and full VAT-section reference, plus technical BIM deliverables register or delivery receipt evidencing offshore performance
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS may retrospectively disallow the zero rating and issue an additional VAT assessment at 15%, recovering the principal VAT together with prescribed interest from the date the refund was anciently claimed. Where fraudulent or negligent misstatement is established, an additional administrative penalty of 200% of the assessed amount applies under section 222(1)(c) of the Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011. Criminal prosecution under the VAT Act and Customs and Excise Act 91 of 1964 may further be instituted, carrying fines up to ZAR 1 million and imprisonment of up to five years for knowingly issuing false zero-rated invoices; export-proceeds default beyond 180 days also triggers exchange-control penalties and repatriation assessments.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB) — Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv), acting under the Currency and Exchanges Act, 1933 (Act No. 9 of 1933), the Exchange Control Regulations, 1961, and the National Payment System Act, 1998 (Act No. 78 of 1998). Day-to-day administration is delegated to Authorised Dealers (licensed commercial banks) under SARB's Exchange Control Manual.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The ZAR is fully convertible for current-account items (exports of services including BIM/CAD engineering, imports, and ordinary remittances) subject to documentary verification by an authorised dealer. Capital-account movements remain controlled: inward FDI in a South African (Pty) Ltd is automatically permitted via share subscription against post-issuance reporting; profit remittance (dividends) is legal but requires audited annual financial statements, a Form A application, transfer-pricing documentation, and a SARS tax-clearance (dividend withholding tax at 20% domestic rate, treaty-reduced under most DTAAs). Non-resident shareholder loans below R100 million per annum are reportable; amounts above that threshold require prior FinSurv approval.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Mandatory surrender/conversion of export proceeds into ZAR was abolished. Full repatriation into South Africa, however, remains compulsory: proceeds from BIM/CAD service invoices must be received through an authorised dealer within 30 days of the performance date (or the permissible exporter term, with 180-day extension approval), and may be credited to a Foreign Currency Account (FCA) in USD/EUR/GBP without a conversion ratio. Each inward service fee must be documented by the underlying contract, SOW, and invoice for SARS and dealer-level invisible-export reporting; failure to repatriate within the statutory window attracts exchange-control penalties.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: HIGH for inbound collection and conversion of third-party project fees through Wise (operating in South Africa via a licensed local arrangement with a domestic commercial bank under the National Payment System Act and PASA rules) — viable up to approximately USD 1–2 million annual service revenue. Two hard constraints apply: (i) an EMI is not an authorised dealer, so all net ZAR settlements must land on a South African bank account within the SARB zonal clearing system; and (ii) dividend remittances, intercompany capital flows, and Form A applications may not be executed through an EMI — they must route via the domestic authorised dealer. Legal risk rises if the Wise collection entity sits in an opaque offshore structure or is used to bypass repatriation rules.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: FICA (Act 38 of 2001) does not mandate a physical interview; in practice the Big Four banks require at least one natural-person director or a notarially appointed authorised signatory to attend an in-branch activation session in Johannesburg, Cape Town, or Durban for the first account opening. Remote onboarding via e-KYC is partially accepted for South African directors of a standard-risk CAD/BIM entity; non-resident directors must provide certified passports, proof of residential address, a notarised Power of Attorney to a local signatory, and a FICA beneficial-ownership resolution identifying every ultimate beneficial owner at or above 25%.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Single-client concentration — nearly all BIM/CAD fees received from one offshore parent or large project client without visible commercial substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master services agreement; project SOWs; BIM model deliverables and transmittal logs; client acceptance emails; group transfer-pricing policy aligned with South African Section 31 rules; UBO organogram; notarised board resolutions approving treasury routing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Invoice-payment mismatch — settlement amounts differing from quoted invoices or arriving from non-contractual third-party originators.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Invoice register with purchase order numbers; reconciliation schedules; subcontractor agreements and payment vouchers; software licensing invoices (e.g., Autodesk, Bentley) and cloud-hosting statements; bank statements; director sworn affidavit explaining settlement flows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual inbound equity injection — a large non-resident share subscription during a period of negligible operating revenue.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Share subscription agreement; parent company proof-of-funds affidavit; bank reference letter; authorised-dealer confirmation of exchange-control notification; SARS tax-clearance certificate; original share certificates; CIPC annual return.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Jurisdictional screening hits — UBO chain passing through FATF grey-listed or sanctioned jurisdictions, or sanctioned counterparties appearing in project deliverables.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions screening report (World-Check / LexisNexis) for all directors, UBOs, and clients; corporate register extracts for each group entity; CIPC and offshore company certificates; external legal opinion confirming no sanctions nexus; complete client onboarding KYC pack.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity route: the non-resident parent subscribes for ordinary shares via SWIFT MT103 using the balance-of-payments code for inward FDI in share capital; the authorised dealer credits the FCA or converts to ZAR, and files the statutory inward-investment notification on the SARB electronic exchange-control reporting channel within 30 days. Supporting records are share certificates, CIPC resolution, tax registration, and proof-of-funds documents. Debt route (intercompany loan below R100 million per annum): MT103 with an intercompany-financing purpose code; the dealer files the foreign-liability return, and the borrower must retain the loan agreement, drawdown schedule, and financial statements evidencing an arm's-length interest rate for SARS Section 31 transfer-pricing and thin-capitalisation compliance.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade and operational payments settle via SWIFT MT103 through the authorised dealer, with a Form A filing for all ZAR-conversion purchases of software licences, cloud infrastructure, subcontracted services, and professional fees. For Southern African (SADC) counterparties, SIRESS (SADC Integrated Regional Electronic Settlement System) provides a regional real-time gross settlement rail. Capital-intensive procurement (e.g., BIM workstations, render farms, or surveying hardware from APAC suppliers) uses irrevocable commercial letters of credit (SWIFT MT700/MT710) with DP/DA documentary collections as secondary instruments; every outward disbursement must cite the underlying contract and invoice to withstand SARB audit.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX forwards (USD/ZAR, EUR/ZAR, GBP/ZAR) up to 24 months against forecast BIM/CAD service-export receivables, executed only through an authorised dealer with documented underlying exposure and no speculative cover.
European-style OTC FX options (call/put on USD/ZAR and EUR/ZAR) with premium payment and matching underlying invoice exposure.

Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) for hedging a material non-resident shareholder loan against ZAR cash-flow volatility — subject to FinSurv approval for tenors beyond authorised-dealer limits.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) against ZAR where the onshore interbank market cannot deliver the currency for the required tenor; route the NDF leg through the authorised dealer's offshore desk or a syndicated hedge desk.
Exchange-traded USD/ZAR futures and options on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) as the most transparent, daily-marked rail for tactical hedging of short-dated service-fee receipts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CIPC Annual Return (CoR 40.1) with confirmation of registered company details
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after each anniversary of the date of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty ZAR 500-1,000 (approximately USD 28-56) per annum; two consecutive un-filed annual returns trigger a CIPC compliance notice and administrative strike-off (deregistration) after the prescribed notice period.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Interest (BOI) Register declaration and shareholding-confirmation update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Update within 7 business days of any share transfer or change in beneficial ownership; annual confirmation submitted together with the CIPC Annual Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Contravention of the General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Terrorism Financing) Amendment Act 22 of 2022 attracts a fine of up to ZAR 1,000,000 (approximately USD 55,000) and/or imprisonment of up to 10 years; a CIPC compliance notice may also be issued.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements (AFS) prepared and, where statutorily triggered, independently reviewed or audited and retained
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: CIPC where filing is required; otherwise retained at the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Prepared within 6 months after the financial year-end; independent review or audit completed within the same 6-month window
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Contravention of the Companies Act 71 of 2008 section 30; CIPC compliance notice, administrative penalties, and potential director liability for failure to prepare and present the annual financial statements.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Submitted within 12 months after the financial year-end, subject to any earlier date prescribed by public notice in the SARS e-filing cycle
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative non-compliance penalty of 10% of assessed tax per month of default (capped at 50% of assessed tax), plus interest at the prescribed rate; criminal prosecution for wilful failure to submit.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A South African (Pty) Ltd must undergo a full independent audit when its Public Interest Score (PIS) is 350 or more; a PIS between 100 and 349 requires an independent review by a registered accountant; a PIS below 100 imposes no statutory audit or review unless required by the Memorandum of Incorporation or a shareholders' resolution. A private company holding assets in a fiduciary capacity above the prescribed threshold is also subject to compulsory audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted in South Africa under the Companies Act 71 of 2008 section 29; IFRS for SMEs is permitted for companies with a Public Interest Score below 350 and for exempt micro enterprises.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Section 50 as amended requires every company to maintain a Beneficial Ownership Register and to file it with CIPC. The annual return confirmation requires directors to verify that the BOI declaration remains complete and accurate; any share-transfer or change in beneficial ownership must be recorded in the register and filed with CIPC within 7 business days. The register must be available for inspection by regulators on request.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Auditors (where an auditor or reviewer is appointed)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300-1,200 per year for registered-office and company-secretarial or compliance-agent services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 800-2,000 for an independent review; USD 2,500-7,000 for a full audit engagement
